BiblicalUsage: This verb for winding or weaving together occurs once, in Micah 7:3: the prince asks, the judge asks for a reward, the great man utters his mischievous desire — 'so they wrap it up.' The word pictures evil being woven, strand by strand, until prince, judge, and great man have twisted it into one finished scheme.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse shows me how corruption works — not in one bold act, but woven together by many hands — and it warns me to watch for the small threads of compromise in my own life.
